claims.text: Introducing 2–5 vol% Y2O3 nanoparticles during deposition can produce a uniform and stable nanoparticle dispersion in the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
Optimized nanoparticle synthesis and pre-annealing treatments will help ensure a uniform and stable Y2O3 dispersion.
Uniformly distributed Y2O3 nanoparticles act as obstacles that pin dislocations.
Y2O3 nanoparticles hinder local plastic flow in the coating.
Dispersed nano-oxides impede dislocation glide during sliding.
Dispersed Y2O3 nanoparticles suppress localized shear-band formation during high-temperature sliding.
Dislocation obstruction by the nanoparticles retards plastic deformation.
Dispersion strengthening elevates the deformation threshold of the coating.
Adding the optimized Y2O3 dispersion reduces the wear rate relative to the nanoparticle-free baseline.
The Y2O3-containing coating will exhibit fewer shear bands than the baseline coating.
The Y2O3-containing coating will exhibit fewer plastic-flow zones than the baseline coating.
The predicted strengthening, deformation suppression, and wear reduction hold during sliding at 600–750°C.
The proposed mechanism applies to thin FeNiCrCoCu coatings on conventional metal substrates.
Prolonged high-temperature exposure may destabilize the nano-oxide dispersion.
Nanoparticle agglomeration may limit the proposed strengthening mechanism.
Nanoprecipitate–dislocation interactions can generate high stress, dislocation accumulation, and hardening in a worn subsurface layer.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant wear-rate reduction and suppression of localized deformation relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The predicted-outcome field says that no significant wear improvement alone would falsify the hypothesis, whereas the formal rule can be read as requiring both no wear-rate reduction and no corresponding suppression of localized deformation. These criteria are not fully aligned.
